Hardie-Ferodo 1000 Mount Panorama, Bathurst 5th October, 1975 Number of Laps: 163 Total Race Time: 7:50:99.1 Fastest lap: Peter Brock, 2:29.8 Classes: Class A - Up to 1300cc; Class B - 1301 to 2000cc; Class C - 2001 to 3000cc; Class D - 3001 to 6000cc 1975 Hardie-Ferodo 1000 Program Even before the 1975 race started, there was a raging controversy about the future of the event following the announcement by the race organisers, the Australian Racing Drivers Club, of their intention to restrict the race to 3-liter cars in 1976. For 1975, the prize money was to be heavily biased towards the classes rather than outright placings, with the follow-up of the complete scrapping of the big cars in 1976. An ARDC official was reported to have said: "It's a race for cars, not drivers,
if Moffat or Goss didn't start I don't think it would be a great loss." This statement was shouted down with some ferocity by motor sport fans
participants,

the idea was dropped. Meanwhile, back at the race track, practice for the 1975 Hardie-Ferodo was going fairly well for Moffat who eventually earned a place on the front row of the grid only one-tenth of a second behind the pole-getter Colin Bond with a time of 2 min 27.4 sec. John Goss's car was blowing smoke all day
could only manage 10th fastest, while the Carter
Winter Falcon grabbed seventh spot. The race itself was not a happy one for Ford, all three Falcons eventually retiring with various maladies, the Goss
Bartlett car blowing its engine after only 10 laps, Carter
Winter suffered a broken oil pipe after 53 laps, while Moffat
Geoghegan, after holding the lead at one stage, had to change a gearbox
then retired with a broken lower control arm. The race was won in easy style by Peter Brock
Brian Sampson in their Gown
Hindaugh Torana L34. Please Note: You can sort this listing by simply clicking on the column heading PLACE DRIVER
